canonical_topic: Eastern Interconnect trading drivers: fuel mix and regional climate
definition: Trading opportunities in the Eastern Interconnect commonly arise from differences in generation fuel mix (coal vs. natural gas) between regions and from north-south differences in seasonal weather patterns.
core_idea: Some of the most significant trades pit coal-heavy regions against gas-heavy regions, while others exploit the fact that the southern Eastern Interconnect has a long summer/mild winter climate whereas the north has cold winters and a shorter cooling season.
key_points: Key trades occur between regions relying on coal-fired generation and regions relying on natural-gas-fired generation
Southern part of the Eastern Interconnect: extended summer, mild winters
Northern part: cold winters, shorter summer air-conditioning season
trading_implications: Coal-vs-gas generation mix differentials across regions create fuel-switching-driven power price spread trades
North-south seasonal demand asymmetry (winter heating vs. summer cooling) creates weather-driven regional spread opportunities
